issues.description: Monkey-patching genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE at import time complects unrelated concerns and silently mutates a third-party global
issues.detail: The line `genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE = 5 * 1024 * 1024` is executed as a side effect of importing pipecat.services.google.llm. This is place-oriented programming at its worst: a mutable global in another library, set unconditionally, affecting every consumer of google-genai in the process — not just users of image models, not just users of this service. The comment literally calls it a 'temporary hack' and ships it. The simple thing is to set this only when the image-capable model is selected, in a scoped way (e.g., via the client's documented config if one exists, or at minimum inside __init__ guarded by model name), and to file/link the upstream issue this is working around. As written, importing this module mutates global state in a dependency for the whole process.

issues.description: OutputImageRawFrame is constructed from raw RGB bytes without converting the PIL image's mode, which will produce wrong pixels for any non-RGB returned image
issues.detail: `Image.open(io.BytesIO(part.inline_data.data))` may return an image in mode RGBA, P, L, CMYK, etc. depending on what the model emits. The code then does `image.tobytes()` and declares `format='RGB'` — but tobytes() returns bytes in the image's *current* mode, not RGB. For an RGBA PNG the byte stream is 4-channel; the consumer interpreting it as 3-channel RGB will get sheared/garbled output. The value (the pixel data) and the identity (the declared format) have been complected and are now lying to each other. Call `image.convert('RGB').tobytes()` before constructing the frame, or pass the actual mode through. Also: nothing handles the case where inline_data carries non-image MIME types (audio, etc.) — the code assumes any inline_data is an image.

issues.description: Changing the default model from gemini-2.0-flash to gemini-2.5-flash is a silent behavior/billing change for every existing caller
issues.detail: The default model parameter on GoogleLLMService.__init__ is the identity callers depend on when they don't pass `model=`. Bumping it in the same PR that adds image support — buried in a feature PR titled 'added support for image generation' — changes pricing, latency, and (with the new thinking-budget logic) reasoning behavior for every existing user who relied on the default. This is essential vs. incidental: the image feature does not require changing the default. Split it into its own changelog entry and ideally its own PR, or at minimum call it out as a breaking-default change in the PR description and release notes more loudly than a one-line 'Changed' entry.

issues.description: Image-model detection by substring 'image' in model name is fragile string-matching standing in for a capability check
issues.detail: `if 'image' in self._model_name` is incidental complexity: the *value* being tested is 'does this model return image parts', but the code is asking a string question that happens to be true today for gemini-2.5-flash-image. Any future model whose name contains 'image' for unrelated reasons (or any image-capable model that doesn't) will silently misbehave. The simple decomposition is a small capability table or a method `_model_supports_image_output(name)` defined in one place, used wherever the question is asked. The thinking-budget branch and the inline_data branch are both implicitly relying on the same fact and should reference the same predicate.

issues.description: Image frames are pushed inside the streaming response loop with no ordering contract relative to text/function-call parts
issues.detail: The new `elif part.inline_data` branch calls `await self.push_frame(frame)` inline while iterating candidate parts, interleaved with text accumulation and function-call collection. There is no explicit model of *when* the image is emitted relative to the surrounding LLMTextFrame stream and the eventual assistant context aggregation — is the image part of the assistant turn? Is it before or after the text it accompanies? Does the context aggregator know an image was produced? This is the time-and-identity question: the assistant's 'value' for this turn is now text + image, but only the text flows into context. Downstream replay/history will silently drop the image. Make the time semantics explicit: either include the image in the assistant context, or document clearly that images are side-channel and not part of conversational history.

issues.description: Dependency specifier widening from `~=` to `>=X,<Y` is a real policy change worth one sentence of rationale
issues.detail: Switching google-genai, google-cloud-speech, and google-cloud-texttospeech from compatible-release (`~=`) to broad `>=,<major` ranges trades reproducibility for flexibility across the whole google extra. That may be the right call, but it's a separable decision from 'add image support' and deserves a line in the PR description explaining why now and what the test coverage is across the new allowed range. Otherwise future breakage inside the allowed range will be blamed on this PR.

issues.description: Example file header says 'Gemini for both LLM, STT and TTS' but uses GoogleSTTService/GoogleTTSService (Google Cloud, not Gemini)
issues.detail: Small but real: the docstring conflates two different products (Gemini API and Google Cloud Speech/TTS). The example also requires GOOGLE_TEST_CREDENTIALS in addition to GOOGLE_API_KEY but only documents the latter in the 'Make sure to set' block. Easy to fix; matters because this file is the canonical onboarding artifact for the feature.

issues.description: Stray blank line added in __init__ with no semantic content
issues.detail: The diff inserts a blank line after `self._http_options = http_options` and before `self._create_client(...)`. Trivial, but it's the kind of incidental churn that shows up in blame forever. Worth removing.

review.summary: This PR adds a real capability (image output from Gemini image models) but ships it with several complected concerns and one genuinely dangerous line. The headline problem is a module-import-time monkey-patch of google-genai's READ_BUFFER_SIZE — a mutable global in someone else's library, set unconditionally for every consumer of pipecat.services.google.llm, labeled 'temporary hack' in the code itself. The second hard problem is that the new image frame is constructed with `image.tobytes()` and `format='RGB'` without converting the PIL image's mode, so any non-RGB returned image will produce wrong pixel bytes. Beyond those: the default model is silently bumped (a value/identity change for every existing caller), image-model detection is string-substring matching standing in for a capability predicate, and there's no explicit time/ordering model for how the emitted image frame relates to the assistant turn's text and conversational history. The decomposition I'd want: a single `_model_supports_image_output()` predicate used in both branches, scoped buffer-size handling (or an upstream fix), explicit `convert('RGB')` before tobytes, and the default-model change pulled into its own PR.
